title: Clothing Defects Kill Brand Loyalty — Survey
paragraphs: When a piece of clothing falls apart too quickly, many shoppers do not complain. Instead, they quietly stop buying from that brand, according to a new report.

The report was published in October by Samsara Eco, an Australian company that develops technology for recycling textiles. It surveyed more than 5,000 consumers around the world, most of them young people interested in sustainable fashion.

The survey found that 27.7% of people would leave a brand after a garment failed. Of these, 15.8% said they would never buy from the brand again, and 11.9% said they would switch to a competitor. Only 2.3% said they would replace the item with one from the same brand. This means people are about 12 times more likely to leave a brand than to buy the same product again.

Very few people tell the brand about the problem. Just 5.9% said they would return a damaged item, so companies may never learn why they are losing customers. Meanwhile, more than 64% said they would repair the item or simply keep wearing it.

The most common problems were fabric becoming thin or developing holes, mentioned by 62% of respondents. This was followed by seams coming apart, at 55%, and pilling, when small balls of fiber form on fabric, at 50%.
Consumers also have clear expectations. About 89% expect to wear a piece of clothing at least 30 times, and 54% said brands are responsible for quality.

Rising living costs are also changing how people shop. Over 88% said the cost of living has affected the way they buy clothes, and about one in three are buying less while expecting more from each item.
However, the results may not represent all shoppers, because the people surveyed were mostly young and interested in sustainability.
